transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-01
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Moreno (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Avalon Procurement), James Orr (Avalon Legal), Priya Singh (Avalon Security), Nora Wells (Avalon AI)

Summary: Procurement kickoff to review MSA/DPA open points, SLA targets, pricing approval path, and next steps for a two-week pilot. Security questions around data residency, KMS, retention and audit logs; legal redlines expected on data indemnity and retention windows. Redwood to provide security artifacts and committed-capacity options.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I think we, um, wanted to get through the MSA/DPA high level, SLA targets that Avalon needs, and iron out timing for the pilot and pricing approval.
[00:18] Maya (Procurement): Thanks Alex. Yes, we're on a tight timeline - our procurement committee wants vendor selection by mid-August. We need to understand pricing buckets and what committed capacity means for our forecasting, also any minimum terms.
[00:35] Alex: Absolutely. Jules will walk through onboarding and pricing later. Samir, do you want to start on the security & deployment options?
[00:44] Samir (SE): Sure. Quick recap: Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployment in a VPC/on-prem model. For Avalon we discussed dedicated pools behind your VPC peering or a private control plane with customer-managed network. For PHI/PII workloads we'd recommend Dedicated or Private to meet isolation and retention controls.
[01:12] Priya (Security): Right - our baseline is we need audit logs forwarded to Splunk, KMS-managed key support (customer keys), and proof of SOC 2 Type II. Also, what's your stance on data residency - our prod tenant must stay in us-east-1.
[01:33] Samir: We can pin region to us-east-1 for the Dedicated cluster; private deployments give you full control. We support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for encryption-at-rest and SSE. Audit logs can be exported and we have an event stream that many customers ship to SIEMs (sometimes the transcription shows 'KV cash' sorry that's the engine's note).
[01:56] Priya: (laughs) okay KV cash, noted. For the DPA, James will have a few redlines on retention and breach notification windows.
[02:05] James (Legal): Yep. Our legal prefers 30-day notice for material changes, 48-hour notification for incidents, and a clear data deletion clause on termination. Also, indemnity cap questions - we may ask for carveouts around gross negligence.
[02:24] Alex: Understood. Our standard MSA includes a 72-hour incident notification SLA in a lot of deals, but we can see if 48 hours is acceptable for you - I'll flag to legal. The DPA typically allows for 30/60/90 day retention tiers; we can propose a shorter retention for sensitive flows.
[02:46] Maya: On pricing, key question: what's the difference in unit economics between Hosted API vs Dedicated Reserved? We need cost per token or per inference estimate for our forecast.
[02:59] Alex: Good question. Hosted API is pay-as-you-go and flexible but slightly higher per-token. Dedicated is committed capacity - we can provide a committed monthly throughput and lower unit cost; there's also burst capacity. Jules, want to speak to the worksheet?
[03:12] Jules (CSM): I'll send a clear worksheet showing three scenarios: 1) Minimal pilot (hosted) 2) Dedicated 8-GPU pool for production forecast and 3) Private on-prem. Each row will include monthly cost, expected latency SLOs, and operational responsibilities. For procurement we usually show straight comparisons so you can run TCO.
[03:36] Leo (Finance): For approval we need clear committed spend options and termination terms. Any early-termination fees?
[03:44] Alex: For Dedicated contracts there's a commitment term; early termination fees vary by length. We'll include standard 12- and 24-month options in the worksheet.
[03:54] Nora (AI Lead): From a technical standpoint, we want to run a 2-week pilot with our sample inference workload - 95th pct latency targets around sub-300ms for short prompts and stable throughput for large batches. Can you support perf testing and share benchmarks?
[04:15] Samir: Yes, we can spin up a dedicated test pool or a hosted benchmark with Redwood's verified models. We'll need your sample prompt distribution and token counts. For batching, caching and quantization tradeoffs we can tune during the pilot. We'll share a benchmarking guide.
[04:36] Maya: Good. Also legal will want to see the DPA redline in advance so we can route it internally. James, do you have specific clauses to expect?
[04:45] James: Mostly retention window, subprocessor list, liability cap, and audit rights. We may ask for SSO/SAML integration timelines and proof of background checks for personnel with access.
[04:58] Samir: We support SAML/SSO and RBAC; background checks are typically covered under our security attestation, and we can provide a list of subprocessors and a SOC 2 report.
[05:12] Maya: On SLAs, we need uptime and response time guarantees for inference - 99.9% availability during business hours at minimum and clear credits for downtime. Are you open to contractual credits?
[05:26] Alex: We offer SLA credits for Dedicated customers; specifics vary by plan. For Hosted customers we have standard credits. We'll include SLA language options and the proposed credit table in the package.
[05:38] Priya: A couple of security questions - do you support VPC peering or PrivateLink? Also, how do you handle logs with PHI?
[05:50] Samir: We support both VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on region. For PHI we recommend encryption with customer KMS and limited retention. Logs that include PHI can be redacted or not stored depending on configuration; we'll include the options and default retention in the security pack.
[06:12] James: On indemnity, Redwood's standard is x times the contract value - we might need a carveout for gross negligence. We'll propose specific language.
[06:24] Alex: Fair. We'll surface your proposed carveouts and see which ones are acceptable to Redwood legal - I can't commit to changes on the spot but we'll engage legal right away.
[06:33] Maya: Process-wise, after you send the DPA and pricing, we will route to procurement committee and legal. If we can get documents by EOW next week, we can have approval by mid-August.
[06:45] Jules: For onboarding, typical timeline: 1) contract signing, 2) kickoff and infra setup (1 week), 3) pilot (2 weeks), 4) production ramp. We'll attach a checklist.
[07:00] Nora: For the pilot, we need guidance on request signing, tokenization, and partial response streaming behavior. Our product must tolerate partial tokens for long sequences.
[07:15] Samir: We support streaming responses and function/tool calling. We'll document how partial streaming works across SDKs. Also note that certain quantized backends may have slightly different latencies on long sequences.
[07:32] Leo: Back to pricing - will you provide list prices and then negotiated committed discounts? We need to know what to put into our budget planning.
[07:44] Alex: Yes, list price + committed discounts depending on term and capacity. We'll show example calculations.
[07:52] Priya: One more - audit rights: can Avalon request an on-site audit or a third-party SOC review?
[08:02] James: We typically ask for SOC 2 and the ability to request a security questionnaire.
[08:07] Samir: We can provide SOC 2 Type II reports and a security questionnaire. On-site audits are generally handled through our security team under NDA; we'll document the process.
[08:20] Maya: Great - what about export controls or data residency for EU patients? We may have some EU nodes later, but initial scope is US-only.
[08:31] Alex: For EU workloads we'd recommend pinning region accordingly or private deployment. For US-only we will ensure the tenant is provisioned in us-east-1.
[08:40] James: Regarding termination, we need clarity on data return/deletion, and a tutorial on how to request data deletion (API endpoints, timelines).
[08:52] Jules: We'll include the steps: request deletion via support portal, confirm within X days, and provide a deletion certificate when completed.
[09:02] Maya: Okay that's helpful. Any blockers on your side for providing those artifacts?
[09:07] Alex: No blockers. Samir can gather the security pack and Jules will assemble the onboarding checklist and pricing worksheet.
[09:16] (longer silence as participants shift)
[09:23] Samir: Quick technical note - for the pilot we recommend a test harness that simulates your peak QPS and tail latency. We'll provide a load script. Also a heads-up: some model names in our catalog are slightly different in the docs; please forgive naming inconsistencies - sometimes the transcript flips letters.
[09:45] Nora: Cool, send the load script and model mapping. We'll prepare our traffic profile.
[09:50] Maya: Timeline recap?
[09:53] Alex: I'll send pricing by Tue (8/4), Samir sends security pack by Wed (8/5), Avalon returns DPA redlines by Tue (8/11). Pilot targeted start 8/10 pending infra.
[10:05] James: Sounds good. I will try to get our legal comments earlier if possible.
[10:10] Maya: A tiny thing - can Redwood accommodate a clause requiring yearly penetration tests and a 3rd party attest?
[10:18] Samir: We already do annual penetration testing and can provide summary reports; full reports are usually redacted. We'll note that.
[10:28] Leo: Budgetly, can you include an option for a capped monthly commitment with a ramp schedule? We want predictability with a growth buffer.
[10:37] Alex: Yes, our dedicated offers can include ramping commitments across quarters - we'll lay out a ramp table in the pricing worksheet.
[10:47] Priya: If we go Private deployment on-prem, what's the estimated lead time?
[10:53] Samir: For on-prem it's longer - packaging, network setup, and cert exchanges typically take 4-8 weeks depending on approvals. We'll put both timelines in the doc.
[11:08] Maya: Any outstanding security docs we should expect beyond SOC 2 and ISO?
[11:13] Samir: We'll include penetration test summary, subprocessors list, DPA, encryption architecture, and KMS integration guide.
[11:22] Nora: For the pilot success criteria: latency SLOs met, throughput >= X rps (we'll provide target), and no data leakage in logs. We'll formalize these.
[11:34] Alex: Great. We'll draft a short SOW for the pilot that includes success criteria and acceptance tests.
[11:42] James: We'll also need a confidentiality addendum for any pre-launch IP sharing.
[11:48] Jules: We can include an NDA/Confidentiality addendum if needed; many customers piggyback on the MSA confidentiality section.
[11:56] Maya: Okay, looks like we're aligned. Any final questions?
[12:00] Samir: None from me.
[12:02] Alex: Thanks everyone - appreciate the clear list of items. We'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[12:12] Maya: Thanks all.

Recap / Close:
- Redwood to deliver: pricing worksheet (committed & burst scenarios), security pack (SOC 2, ISO, pen test summary), DPA template, pilot SOW and onboarding checklist.
- Avalon to deliver: sample workload profile, internal DPA comments, security control list.
- Target timeline: docs by 2026-08-05, pilot start ~2026-08-10, procurement decision mid-August.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hears (e.g., KV cache noted as KV cash), speaker labels auto-attributed at times.

End of recording.
